data.title: Treasury Yields Fall as Anthopic Fails to Sustain Risk Appetite — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Paulo Trevisani and Emese Bartha

U.S. Treasury yields turned lower Thursday following the Anthropic IPO.

The AI company priced its shares at $83, giving it a value of up to $1.5 trillion. Once they started trading on the Nasdaq, the shares rose nearly 20%. But it wasn't enough to revive risk appetite across financial markets and investors again sought the safety of bonds, driving yields lower.

"Risk-off is really the sentiment," Andrew Wells, chief investment officer at SanJac Alpha said. "I think we're seeing that kind of play out with Anthropic's IPO opening," as the initial euphoria cooled down during the trading session, he said.

Weakness in equities, in turn, could have implications for monetary policy.

"The deepening correction in tech stocks-which was unrelieved by the record-smashing IPO-is casting some doubt on just how much further the [Federal Reserve] will tighten," BMO's chief economist Douglas Porter said. "While Fed officials continue to sound quite hawkish, softening equities will tighten financial conditions and could limit the extent of rate hikes."

Meanwhile, weekly jobless claims unexpectedly increased. The Leading Economic Index, or LEI, published by research group The Conference Board, slid 0.3% to 99.3 after sitting unchanged in September.

The Treasury auctioned $19 billion in inflation-protected securities, or TIPS, paying a yield of 2.903%, the highest since 2002.

Treasury yields gave up early increases and traded lower. The 10-year slipped to 5.051% from 5.065%, while the two-year decreased to 4.777% from 4.798%.

Eurozone bond yields were slightly higher ahead of heavy bond supply from Spain and France. Spain will auction 4.5 billion euros to 5.5 billion euros ($4.94 billion to $6.04 billion) in three bonds, including a new seven-year maturity. France will offer a combined 11.25 billion euros to 13.75 billion euros in a total of eight nominal and inflation-linked bonds.

The 10-year German Bund yield edged up 0.036 percentage point to 3.420%, according to Tradeweb.

Minutes of the latest Fed rate-setting meeting, where the Fed left interest rates unchanged, indicated that some policymakers are leaning toward a larger-than-usual increase of half a percentage point in December. The committee's discussion of inflation revealed increasing concern of broadening price pressure amid strong growth in economic activity, Stuart Paul, U.S. economist at UBS, said in a note.

The minutes increased market expectations of a 50-basis-point Fed rate hike at the December meeting. Money markets currently price in a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point hike in December and an 8% likelihood of a 50-basis-point tightening, according to LSEG. A 50-basis-point hike was priced with a 2% probability on Wednesday.

"An unyielding Federal Reserve continues to govern fixed income and currency markets," Patrick Munnelly, market strategist at Tickmill Group, said in a note. "Wednesday's October [Federal Open Market Committee] minutes confirmed that nearly all officials anticipate further rate hikes to return inflation to target, with two participants even floating the risk of a 50bps move in December if price pressures persist," he said.

Crucially, policymakers took comfort from tighter market-implied rate paths doing the Fed's heavy lifting--meaning any sustained AI-driven easing in financial conditions risks provoking a sharper monetary pushback, Munnelly added.

Write to Paulo Trevisani at paulo.trevisani@wsj.com and to Emese Bartha at emese.bartha@wsj.com

data.title: Mitsubishi Power wins turbine order for Vietnam's O Mon 3
data.description:
Can Tho, a city in the south of Vietnam, is home to O Mon 3, a 1,155MW combined cycle power plant that will receive two M701JAC gas turbines from Mitsubishi Power, the Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (7011) brand said on its website. Scheduled for completion in 2030, the facility should help strengthen the power supply in the country's southern region.

With this latest deal, the Japanese group will provide a total of four M701JAC units for O Mon 3 and the adjacent O Mon 4, which deepens its involvement in the O Mon Power Complex. The two plants are both part of the Block B-O Mon chain, which converts gas into electricity and which Vietnam regards as a national priority for securing its energy needs and moving to cleaner sources.

Mitsubishi Power (7011) secured the turbine order together with Doosan Enerbility. Doosan Enerbility, from South Korea, has teamed up with Vietnam's Petrovietnam Technical Services Corporation (PTSC) in the consortium that holds the O Mon 3 contract covering engineering, procurement and construction. That contract was awarded by Petrovietnam, as the state-owned Vietnam National Industry - Energy Group is known.

'We are honored to bring our advanced JAC gas turbine technology to O Mon 3, building on our involvement in O Mon 4. The four units to be supplied across these two power plants reflect our continued commitment toward Vietnam's energy and economic development'

'We look forward to working closely with Petrovietnam and our partners to ensure the successful delivery of the project, and contribute to world-class reliability and efficiency,' Akihiro Ondo, CEO and Managing Director of Mitsubishi Power Asia Pacific Pte. Ltd said.

In August 2025, Mitsubishi Power signed a deal to provide two of the same turbine model for O Mon 4, which also has a capacity of 1,155MW. Three months later, in November 2025, the company announced a separate contract to help convert the O Mon 1 Thermal Power Plant from oil to natural gas.

The company said its J-Series Air-Cooled turbines have reached combined cycle efficiency above 64% and have logged more than 3.7mn operating hours around the world.

data.title: LatAm stocks hit one-year low, FX slips on tighter Fed bets
data.description:
Key points:
  • LatAm currencies hit 10 month low
  • Brazil Senate backs fiscal package, easing debt concerns
  • Mexico data signals resilience despite peso's recent weakness

By Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Avinash P

MSCI’s index of Latin American equities slipped to a one-year low on Thursday amid fragile global sentiment, while growing expectations of tighter US interest rates weighed on regional currencies.‌

The index (.MILA00000PUS) fell 2.72% to its weakest since late November 2025.

"These don't seem like fundamental bottom-up moves. It seems like short-term macro sentiment, which is creating high levels of correlation across different asset classes," said Malcolm Dorson, head of EM strategy at Global X.

"Fed governors, including Governor Waller, have said inflation remains heading in the wrong direction. So it’s not just emerging markets. Risk assets in general have been on edge."

Brazil's benchmark Bovespa index fell 1% as losses in the energy sector weighed on the benchmark.

Investors also assessed the Brazil Senate's approval of a fiscal package aimed at meeting the government's fiscal targets, although many viewed the measures as only an initial step toward improving the country's debt outlook.

Brazilian President Lula da Silva criticized market participants for profiting from speculation over his cabinet picks. Brazilian assets have sold off since his reelection.

Brazil's real slipped 0.9% to a fresh April 2025 low.

The broader index of Latin American currencies (.MILA00000CUS) fell 1.96% to a 10- month low.

Investors have largely priced in a quarter-point rate hike from the Federal Reserve in December, helping lift the dollar to multi-month highs and putting pressure on emerging-market currencies across the board.

A stronger dollar weighs on developing-market currencies by drawing capital into US assets and away from riskier markets.‌

In Mexico, the peso fell 1.5% against the US dollar as investors weighed the widening monetary policy divergence between the Federal Reserve and the Bank of Mexico after the Fed raised interest rates in September for the first time in three years, while Banxico delivered a quarter-percentage-point rate cut earlier this month.

Despite the currency's weakness, data from national statistics agency INEGI pointed to resilience in Mexico's economy, with a preliminary estimate showing economic activity likely expanded 2.3% in October from a year earlier.

Chile's peso fell 0.7%, though analysts pointed to upside potential for the currency.

"We have a bullish view on the Chilean peso. This is our preferred strategy in a scenario of falling global oil prices. Risks are weaker copper prices, US tariffs on refined copper, and lower-than-expected economic growth," said Ezequiel Aguirre, head of LatAm FX and rates strategy at BofA Global Research.

In the US, Anthropic briefly topped a $2 trillion market valuation in its market debut, but initial enthusiasm waned as concerns over the durability of the AI trade, which has driven sentiment recently, weighed on risk appetite.

Elsewhere, Ukraine's bonds also weakened, highlighting lingering investor concerns over geopolitical risks despite signs of progress on the diplomatic front.​‌​‌

Separately, South Africa's central bank held its key interest rate in a split decision, with its governor saying monetary policy was tight enough after two hikes this year.

data.title: What to Know About CEO Dario Amodei — WSJ
data.description:
By Kevin T. Dugan

Dario Amodei was raised in the San Francisco area, competing in academic decathlons and physics olympiads-contests he often fell short of winning.

"My penchant for second place finishes is legendary," he wrote in a bio for the U.S. Physics Olympiad when he was a teenager. The young Dario also said he enjoyed Isaac Asimov-"the greatest Sci-Fi writer of all time," in his estimation-whose stories wrestled with the implications of thinking machines.

More about the Anthropic CEO:

  • He received a doctorate in biophysics, and his early postgraduate work at the Stanford School of Medicine focused on cancer research.
  • After working at Baidu and Google, he was recruited by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman in 2016 over dinner at an Indian restaurant, according to the New Yorker.
  • Eventually, the two found themselves at odds over AI's dangers. In December 2020, he and six others left to start their own frontier lab.

Read more here on the Anthropic co-founders.

data.title: Prized teams from collapsing law firm Weil join Sullivan & Cromwell, Milbank
data.description:
By Sara Merken

Teams of lawyers from Weil, Gotshal & Manges are joining Sullivan & Cromwell and Milbank, adding to the growing diaspora of Weil lawyers amid the 95-year-old law firm's dissolution.

Sullivan & Cromwell on Thursday said at least 12 lawyers will join in New York from Weil's highly regarded restructuring practice, including Gary Holtzer, a former leader of the group, and current US restructuring co-chair Ronit Berkovich.

Weil partners Kelly DiBlasi and Jessica Liou, as well as counsel Alejandro Bascoy, will also join Sullivan & Cromwell as partners in its restructuring and special situations group, the firm said.

Meanwhile, Milbank said on Thursday that it will launch in Paris with Weil's entire team there, comprising 22 partners and 87 lawyers in total. The group includes David Aknin, who will be global co-head of Milbank's private equity practice, and Yannick Piette, who will serve as global co-head of its public M&A practice.

Law firms have been heavily recruiting Weil lawyers since the firm first said in late October that it planned to wind down following a string of key partner departures in recent months. The moves announced this week extended into Weil's core restructuring practice, which had been a major revenue driver for the firm.

Skadden said on Wednesday it was adding a team of about 40 restructuring and corporate lawyers from Weil, including 11 partners. Matt Barr, who led Weil's restructuring practice, will become the head of Skadden's global restructuring group, the firm said.

Several other law firms, including Kirkland & Ellis and Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher, have picked up large teams from Weil. Sidley Austin on Wednesday said it hired 14 partners as part of a 35-lawyer group in New York, across multiple practice areas. Simpson Thacher, Cleary Gottlieb and Latham & Watkins are among the growing list of other firms that have brought on Weil attorneys so far.

Sullivan & Cromwell co-chairs Robert Giuffra and Scott Miller in a statement said the Weil team joining the firm "has advised on many of the largest and most complex chapter 11 cases, cross-border restructurings and liability management transactions of the past two decades."

Sullivan & Cromwell on Thursday separately announced that partners Carsten Berrar and Sharon Nelles will succeed Giuffra and Miller as the firm's leaders in 2028.

data.title: Oil Futures End Volatile Session Near Flat — 4th Update
data.description:
By Farhan Rafid and Anthony Harrup

Oil futures were little changed Thursday at the end of a session of ups and downs as renewed concerns about possible escalation in the Middle East are tempered by improving global supply.

Brent crude for January delivery gained three cents to $91.98 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude for December delivery slipped 0.1% to $83.21 ahead of Friday's contract expiry.

"While the near-term rise in geopolitical tensions is bringing some buying back to crude, the overall fundamentals are still moving more bearish," BOK Financial's senior vice president of trading Dennis Kissler said in a note.

The absence of any breakthrough announcements following the meeting of Presidents Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin has left investors so far with more questions than answers about various conflicts, StoneX senior commodities economist Mike Castle said in a note.

The three leaders agreed to work to reduce nuclear risks and to increase the supply of refined petroleum products, according to a joint statement.

"What the market cares most about and has not seen, however, were any takeaways regarding the push for a diplomatic end to the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East and between Russia/Ukraine, China/U.S. trade and/or technology restrictions, or changes to Russian sanctions," Castle said.

Both crude benchmarks have fallen around 15% so far this month as Trump has held off on renewed large-scale strikes against Iran. A broader retreat across commodity markets and a stronger U.S. dollar have also added to pressure on oil prices.

"The oil market has become acclimated to periodic flareups, just as long as there is no return to all-out war," said Raymond James investment strategist Pavel Molchanov. "With oil production among OPEC's Persian Gulf members having reached 87% of pre-war levels, the industry is gradually adapting."

But the lack of a U.S.-Iran deal "still translates into a hefty risk premium," he added.

Disruptions to Russian refineries have added to the availability of crude for export, even as attacks on energy infrastructure constrain refined fuel supplies. ING analysts said Ukrainian strikes have affected facilities with combined processing capacity of nearly 400,000 barrels a day, while Russian crude exports have climbed to their highest since late July.

Meanwhile, the International Energy Agency said Thursday that prolonged disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz could substantially reduce the world's reliance on the waterway over the next decade as Middle Eastern producers develop alternative export routes.

In its World Energy Outlook, the agency said oil flows through the strait could decline from around 20 million barrels a day before the conflict to 8.5 million barrels a day by 2030 and fewer than 2 million by 2035 under a scenario in which severe shipping disruptions persist.

The agency said the Middle East would remain the world's largest oil-exporting region even under that scenario, as investment in new pipelines and alternative supply routes helps producers maintain access to international markets.

The IEA expects the global oil market to record a surplus of around 1.7 million barrels a day in the fourth quarter, widening to approximately 3.8 million barrels a day next year as Middle Eastern production recovers faster than demand.

The outlook comes amid continued security threats to regional oil infrastructure and shipping, which have complicated efforts to restore exports through the Strait of Hormuz.

data.title: Deluxe Accelerates Payments Integrations from Weeks to Hours
data.description:
Deluxe Corporation (), a trusted payments and data company, today announced the launch of new tools to help software engineers using the developer.deluxe.com portal to integrate with the Deluxe payments system faster than ever.

The upgraded portal provides several key capabilities to the millions of merchants, including retailers and service companies, for which Deluxe processes payments:

  • Model Context Protocol (MCP) access, agent instructions, and tested prompts for AI development tools – including GitHub Copilot, Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI Codex, and Anysphere’s Cursor – work directly with Deluxe APIs and documentation.
  • Enhanced, machine-readable API specifications and technical guidance help developers and AI agents discover relevant payment capabilities, identify integration requirements, and generate implementation code to expedite launch.
  • An interactive sandbox demo, available with try-it-now features, along with embedded search-and-query AI functions.
  • Secure authentication, access management, and implementation best practices help partners build resilient payment experiences.

“Work that once took engineers weeks can now be completed in hours, and AI agents can handle much of the integration,” said Kevin Jones, who is president of Deluxe Merchant Services, the division of Deluxe that supports transactions at millions of businesses, including retailers and service companies. “That is the kind of practical innovation that helps our software partners bring new digital commerce experiences to market faster.”

The upgrades build on the Deluxe Payments Platform (DPP), an API-first foundation for embedded payments and AI-enabled innovation. The enhanced developer experience helps software providers integrate Deluxe payment capabilities more efficiently, supporting faster development and deployment of new payment experiences.

About Deluxe

Deluxe, a trusted payments and data company, champions business so communities thrive. Our solutions help businesses pay, get paid, and grow. For more than 100 years, Deluxe customers have relied on our solutions and platforms at all stages of their lifecycle, from start-up to maturity. Our powerful scale supports millions of small businesses, thousands of vital financial institutions and hundreds of the world’s largest consumer brands, while processing more than $2 trillion in annual payment volume. Our reach, scale, and distribution channels position Deluxe to be our customers’ most trusted business partner. To learn how we can help your business, visit us at www.deluxe.com.

data.title: Sugar futures sink as funds liquidate long positions
data.description:
Sugar futures on ICE fell sharply on Thursday, with New York raw sugar prices losing nearly 5%, as funds liquidated a large part of their long positions to pocket profits before end-of-year books' squaring.

Robusta coffee, meanwhile, fell to a fresh 2-1/2 year low.

SUGAR

* Raw sugar settled down 0.88 cent, or 4.9%, at 17.16 cents per lb after setting a near two-month low of 17.13 cents.

* Dealers said funds have been scaling back a net long position in raw sugar with the market looking technically bearish after breaking below key support levels.

* "We had that 18 cent support level for a while, and when it broke I think several (sell) stops were triggered," said Murilo Barros de Mello, trading director at Hedgepoint Global Markets.

* He believes financial investors decided to pocket gains before the end of the year, but thinks the liquidation is mostly done as fundamentals are not bearish, in general, with production problems in several countries.

* On news, Pakistan's state trading agency TCP is believed to have sold about 96,000 metric tons of white sugar in an international tender seeking to sell and export up to 108,000 tons, which closed last week.

* White sugar lost 3.7% to $488.20 a metric ton.

COFFEE

* Robusta coffee settled down $41, or 1.4%, at $2,978 a ton after setting a 2-1/2 year low of $2,945.

* Dealers said the flow of newly harvested robusta beans from Vietnam had contributed to the recent decline in prices while the recent weakness of Brazil's real had encouraged exports from the world's top coffee producer.

* "Expectations of increased global supplies are weighing on prices with the Vietnam harvest underway and the weak Brazilian real encouraging exports," said a trader based in Vietnam.

* Brazil's currency fell to its lowest level since April 2025 on Thursday.

* Arabica coffee rose 0.2% to $2.76 per lb.

* Colombia coffee production is expected to rebound in the new season, said the USDA on Thursday.

COCOA

* London cocoa ​​settled up £145, or 3.7%, at £4,036 per ton.

* Dealers said low port arrivals in top grower Ivory Coast had helped to underpin the market with the El Niño weather event set to curb global production in the 2026/27 season.

* Ecuador exports could fall by as much as 10% in 2027 because of heavy rains linked to the El Niño, the head of the country's cocoa exporters' association said on Thursday.

* Ample availability of cocoa from the 2025/26 crop, however, continued to keep a lid on prices with exchange stocks well above year-ago levels.

* New York cocoa gained 4% to $5,201 a ton.

data.title: Treasuries Move Modestly Higher After Recovering From Initial Pullback
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Treasuries gave back ground in early trading on Thursday but have shown a notable turnaround over the course of the session.

Bond prices have climbed well off their worst levels of the day and into positive territory. As a result, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, has dipped 1.8 basis points to 5.048 percent.

With the downturn, the ten-year yield has moved lower for the fourth straight day, pulling back further off its highest levels in a month.

The strength that emerged among treasuries may have reflected bonds' appeal as a safe haven as selling pressure intensified on Wall Street.

After turning in a mixed performance early in the day, stocks showed a significant move to the downside soon after intelligence company Anthropic (ANT) made its debut on the Nasdaq.

While the Claude developer priced its initial public offering at a higher-than-expected $83 per share and soared by nearly 40 percent as it began trading, the stock has pulled back well off its highs since then.

The pullback by Anthropic and the subsequent sell-off on Wall Street has partly been attributed to profit taking amid lingering concerns about where the AI trade goes from here.

In U.S. economic news, the Labor Department released a report showing first-time claims for U.S. unemployment benefits unexpectedly edged slightly higher in the week ended November 14th.

The report said initial jobless claims inched up to 203,000, an increase of 1,000 from the previous week's revised level of 202,000.

Economists had expected jobless claims to slip to 198,000 from the 200,000 originally reported for the previous week.

With the unexpected uptick, jobless claims reached their highest level since hitting 207,000 in the week ended September 5th.

data.title: U.S. data center count dwarfs the rest of the world combined
data.description:
The United States now accounts for 5,044 data centers as of October 2026, more than eight times the 595 facilities in the United Kingdom, the next-highest total worldwide.

The gap is even wider in aggregate: the combined data center counts of the following nine countries still fall short of the U.S. figure alone.

This concentration of capacity is drawing fresh scrutiny on the day Anthropic completes its public listing, an event that has focused attention on the artificial intelligence sector and the physical infrastructure required to train and run large models. Germany ranks third with 580 centers, followed by China (443), France (401), India (338), Australia (337), Canada (299), Italy (273), and Japan (269).

Compiled from Data Center Map via Statista and visualized by Arbor Data Science, the rankings highlight the United States as the clear epicenter of digital infrastructure.

As AI systems become more compute-intensive, the geographic skew positions American facilities at the center of model development and deployment. The same concentration also intensifies questions around power demand, cooling requirements, and the competitive landscape as other nations seek to expand their own capacity.

data.title: Nvidia emerges as biggest Intel holder in Q3 despite cutting stake by 25%
data.description:
Chip major Intel saw a mixed response from hedge funds and institutional holders in the third quarter, with several funds adding and divesting their stakes, but none exited their positions in the firm.

Nvidia was the biggest holder of Intel this quarter despite decreasing its stake to 161.08M from 214.78M, or 25% in the second quarter. It accounted for 40% of the fund’s total holdings, falling just behind SpaceX .

George Soros-owned Soros Fund increased its stake in the company to 2.38M shares from 100K shares, while Tiger Global perked up its holdings to 5.54M from 4.25M, translating to a 30% sequential rise. A similar increase was seen in Coatue Management’s portfolio, which boosted its Intel holdings to 15.65M shares from 12.08M last quarter. Maveric Capital expanded its holdings in the firm by 41% Q/Q to 5.17M shares.

Steve Mandel-owned Lone Pine and Rob Citrone-owned Discovery Capital initiated positions in the semiconductor giant with 5.99M and 172,500 shares, respectively, worth 720.69M and 20.74M each. Intel accounted for 4.7% and 1% of the funds’ total portfolio, in the same order.

Softbank maintained its holdings in Intel at 86.96M shares worth $10.45B. Accounting for 64% of its total portfolio, it occupied the top spot among Softbank’s total holdings.
